_comment: Kimi — the product-discovery conversation on the homepage. Flags and every visitor-facing string live here so marketing can change the words and the team can switch a piece off without touching next/kimi-flow.js. {name}, {first}, {email}, {product}, {need}, {capability} are filled at render time. The on-page persona stays 'Stagwell AI'; Kimi is the internal name of the conversation engine and the primary model behind it.

flags._pointersNote: Way-finding under the questions (§4e in KIMI.md). Off at the client's request (2026-09-10): products are named once, at step 6 — the recommendation — and the fast-track form has no skip link. Turn on to show the running under each question and the skip link on the form.
flags._emailNote: WHERE THE EMAIL SITS (client, 2026-09-16: "be flexible with where the email is put … there are no hard rules right now, we'll play with it until we make all the stakeholders happy"). emailFirst true asks for the work email as the second step, reads its domain and skips the website question when the address is a company's own; a free address (gmail, outlook, …) is kept and the website is asked next. false puts the email back after the recommendation, the order of 2026-09-10. phoneStep true asks for a number inline after the email; false leaves the number to the moments where a person is actually being asked for — Book a call, Call my phone, the contact form (client, 2026-09-16: "it's just when they click contact us or book us that they get asked the extra questions about phone number, name").
flags._showcaseNote: THE VALUE BEFORE THE QUALIFICATION (client, 2026-09-16: "as soon as we ask for the email, then we need to provide value before we do anything else"). The order is 1) what you need 2) your email 3) one or more products that fit 4) the details — the business, the size, who they are in the company. showcaseAfterEmail true draws the cards into their own bubble the moment the address step is behind us, and the questions carry on underneath them; the full recommendation, refined by those answers, still comes at the end with the call. false is the old order, where nothing is shown until every question has been asked.
flags._exploreNote: How many taps deep the product detour may go before only the way back is offered. 0 turns it off.

The address is still asked for at the end, by the form, when they want the write-up.
copy.emailWhy: I'll only use the domain — it tells me what your company does, so what I show you is built around your business instead of marketing in general. Worth ten seconds?
copy.emailSkipped: That's fine — we'll carry on without it. If it would help later on, you'll have the chance to share more.
copy.emailSkippedGoal: That's fine — we'll carry on without it. If it would help later on, you'll have the chance to share more. So: what are you trying to solve? Pick one of these, or tell me in a sentence.
copy._showcaseCopyNote: The first look at the products, shown before the business questions (flags.showcaseAfterEmail). showcaseAfter sets the expectation that it gets sharper — the full recommendation follows at the end.

copy.showcaseAfter: Two or three quick things about your business and I'll tighten this up.
copy._exploreNote: GOING DEEPER ON ONE PRODUCT (client, 2026-09-17: 'we dont want to simply reproduce the whole page in the chat window, we want it to be dynamic, and iterative, and animated, and let the user click things and ask questions'). SAIKIMI.explore() walks data/explainers.json one node at a time — the same file the product page renders from. exploreInvite is the line under the cards that offers the detour; the chip* lines are the pills. flags.exploreMaxDepth caps how deep it goes before it offers only the way out. The root step leads with copy.explore.root — the explainer's own `summary` — and shows the differentiators straight away, rather than asking what they would like to know.

On this page, the assistant asks a few questions about what you are trying to solve and recommends the Stagwell AI product that fits, then connects you with the right team.

voice._note: Chat with me (client, 2026-09-11; KIMI-VOICE-PLAN.md). Every visible string of the voice session, and the two lines the model is handed out-of-band (timeUp, back). Start over replaces the session, so there is no 'restarted' line. The agent's own brief is api/_lib/voice/instructions.js.
voice.introduction: Welcome to Stagwell AI. I'm NewVoices — a revolutionary AI voice agent that is changing how brands and companies interact with their customers.
voice.invite: What can I help you with today? Ask me anything — or tap one of the questions below.

starters._note: The opening in two beats (client, 2026-09-11: 'the timing here was too fast … give them an opportunity to say something first'). The agent greets — introduction + invite — and STOPS. These questions appear as animated pills under its words; hero is the focused one that starts the Stagwell AI story (showcase). A tap on a question is the visitor's own words to the agent (step 1: what they want to solve).
questions: How do I improve my AI search results?
How do I find influencers to help promote my product?
How do I keep up to date on what my competitors are doing?
How do I measure whether my brand campaigns are working?

showcase._note: The Stagwell AI story (client, 2026-09-11: 'a banger, awesome opening statement … very visual, with something flying out and another thing coming in … list another product, explain what it does … then talk about how we want to work with the customer'; then: 'pace it slower … before going into detail, tell the user they can interrupt'). Told ON REQUEST — the hero pill, or the visitor asking what Stagwell AI is — never unasked. The agent says interrupt → flagship → each product line → pivot, slowly; voice-stage.js animates to the transcript as it arrives — a product's tile (with its lockup) flies in the moment its name is said; openOn is the word in the transcript that raises the stage when the story was asked for by voice. Every line is the catalog's claim in fewer words; ids must be active products; images must exist.
showcase.interrupt: Before I go into it — interrupt me any time with a question. I'd rather answer you than talk at you.
showcase.flagship: You're talking to one of the flagship AI products from Stagwell AI — and I'm in good company.

products.line: NewIntel — what your competitors did this week, not last quarter.
QuestBrand — always-on brand tracking against the competitors you name.
The Targeting Machine — your first-party data, turned into audiences you can buy.
IMAI — influencer programs end to end, from discovery to ROI.

showcase.more: And that's four of them — plus over ten other AI services, to help with all your business needs.
showcase.moreLine: Explore the whole, growing family of Stagwell AI products.
showcase.peekHint: Hover a member to meet them — tap to read more.
showcase._landNote: WHERE THE STORY PUTS THEM DOWN (client, 2026-09-16: 'once we get to this point we need to pitch to get the customer's email and then to ask them what problem they want to solve with pills'). The story ends on the ASK, not on the question: the agent pitches the address and what it buys them, the composer goes to email, and only once that is answered — or turned down — does it ask what they want to solve, with the six starting points as pills. `closeOn` must be a phrase inside `land`: it is what lifts the pictures away.
showcase.land: One thing before we dig in — what's your work email? I'll read your company's site from it, so everything I tell you next is about you, not about marketing in general.
showcase.closeOnNote: the words in `land` that lift the stage
showcase.landSkip: No problem — we can do it the other way round.

voice.typeIt: Type it in the box below — spelling matters here
voice.cantHear: Not hearing you? Check the mic isn't muted, or type below.
voice.consent: Voice is transcribed on screen so you can read it and so the right team can follow up.
voice.mutedSilence: Muted after a quiet spell — tap to carry on
voice.ended: Voice ended — carry on typing, or start it again.

unavailable.denied: The microphone was not allowed — carry on typing, or allow it and try again.
unavailable.nomic: No microphone was found — carry on typing.
unavailable.busy: Voice is rate-limited while it's in beta, and the limit was just hit — try again in a few minutes, or carry on typing.
unavailable.unconfigured: Voice is not available here yet — carry on typing.
unavailable.network: Voice could not connect — carry on typing, or try again.
unavailable.dropped: Voice dropped — carry on typing, or tap Chat with me to reconnect.

voice.resumed: That was background noise, not the visitor. Carry on from exactly where you stopped, in the same sentence. Do not greet them, do not start again and do not repeat what you have already said.
voice.timeUp: Time is nearly up: say in one line that the rest is quicker to type, then stop.
voice.back: You are reconnected. Say one short line that you are back, then continue with the current step.

copy._emailFreeNote: The line that leads INTO the website question, so it must not ask it: present() puts the question's own prompt straight after this, and the old wording ended '— what's your website?', which came out as 'what's your website? What's your website? I'll take a quick look…' (2026-09-17).
copy._exploreInviteNote: ONE ASK PER SCREEN (client, 2026-09-17: "now I have conflicting funnels… I feel a little lost"). The card used to carry a line and three pills of its own while the question underneath asked for something else entirely — two funnels on one screen. The offer is now a single chip sitting on the QUESTION's own row, beside its answers, so there is one turn, one row and one box.
